facts.fact: The National Identification Authority's homepage says L.I. 2523 requires identity to be authenticated biometrically against the National Identity Register, with institutions onboarded by direct service agreement and a taskforce monitoring compliance.
facts.system: NIA biometric verification against the National Identity Register

GHA.note: The Births and Deaths Registry is named only as a consulted body on date-of-birth updates.

facts.fact: The NIA homepage says the National Identification Authority was established by the National Identification Authority Act, 2006 (Act 707) to create and maintain Ghana Cards.
The NIA homepage says L.I. 2523, the National Identity Register (Amendment) Regulations, 2026, requires identity to be authenticated biometrically against the National Identity Register.
The NIA homepage says L.I. 2523 of 2026 bars organisations from relying on photocopies or scans of the Ghana Card and makes them verify identity biometrically, with penalties for non-compliance.

GHA.note: The registration statistics did not render; no count or share stated.
Only registration of children aged 6-14 is stated, not a number at birth.

facts.fact: The NIA homepage describes the National Identification Authority as a statutory body established by Act 707 to create, maintain, provide and promote the Ghana Card, running registration and verification itself.

GHA.note: No register keyed on the number is named; the NHIS number is only requested alongside.

facts.fact: The NIA homepage says the National Identification Authority issues the Ghana Card, a chip card, against the National Identity Register, and has registered children aged 6-14 in several regions.

The NIA homepage says institutions must verify identity biometrically against the National Identity Register under L.I. 2523, onboarding by service agreement with NIA, and that the NIA taskforce has begun full compliance monitoring.

GHA.note: Nothing on public discussion of government policy.
